# Native Tanach + Existing Range-Reference Revelation

The Awtsmoos has revealed that the missing Chitas reader does not require another Torah store;
Awtsmoos.com already keeps the Written Torah as book series, chapter posts, and one pasuk per section at the native reader's door.

## New hard evidence

- `theWrittenTorah` contains the canonical Tanach book series, including `bereishis`, `shemos`, `vayikra`, `bamidbar`, and `devarim`.
- `devarim` contains 34 posts, exactly its 34 chapters; `bereishis` contains 50 posts, exactly its 50 chapters.
- Devarim chapter 31 is the 31st post in the series and its `dayuh.sections` contains one Hebrew pasuk per array entry.
- Bereishis chapter 1 has the same shape.
- The post metadata records canonical provenance such as `sourceBookTitle`, `sourceChapter`, and `canonicalHebrew`.
- The entity-universe range-reference engine already models living source windows and source comment pointers, but its entity store is currently empty and its two-end selector does not yet select an ordered contiguous span.
- The unfinished Torah Library `/search/library/browse` client is not backed by the currently running local API and must not become a Chitas dependency.
- Native post reader bootstrap loads a post object, manifests it, then starts normal comments/discussion/translation. Therefore a synthetic Chitas post should enter at `coordinates.js`, not fork the reader.

## Revised architecture

1. Keep the existing entity range-reference engine and improve contiguous range semantics generically.
2. Add a browser-side `post-range` compositor that treats ordinary persisted posts as canonical range sources without copying them into entity storage.
3. A Tanach reference such as `Deuteronomy 31:20-31:30` maps deterministically to `devarim`, chapter indexes 31→31, and verse indexes 20→30.
4. Cross-chapter references fetch only the required chapter posts and concatenate only the required section slices.
5. Each composed section carries source metadata: heichel, series, source post id, chapter, verse, and stable `verseSection`.
6. `coordinates.js` intercepts only `seriesId === daily-chitas` + `postId === chitas-YYYY-MM-DD`, synthesizes a normal post, then the existing reader/comments pipeline continues unchanged.
7. Chitas list cards become ordinary internal post cards. `externalHref`, Chabad host allowlisting, and `virtualStudy` social suppression disappear.
8. Week/date/language state is URL-addressable. The canonical Torah source remains Hebrew; English UI is supported immediately, while actual English Torah text may use the existing reader translation layer when available rather than fabricating a translation.
9. A Chitas masthead is a small reader extension above native Torah text, not a parallel page.
10. Comments for the dynamic post remain normal Awtsmoos comments; source verse metadata is retained so a future source-comment jump can reuse the existing range-reference comment pointer model.

## Exact first implementation files

New small modules under `geelooy/heichelos/post/logic/chitas/`: `books.js`, `rangeParser.js`, `postRangeLoader.js`, `dynamicPost.js`, `weekState.js`, `masthead.js`.

Rewrite current `coordinates.js` to delegate daily-chitas resolution before persisted series/post fetch. Rewrite Chitas `schedule.js`, `hebcal-provider.js`, `virtual-series.js`, and Living Path `cards.js` as complete files. Rewrite `postManifest.js` only to call the masthead extension before ordinary post body rendering. Extend server `rangeReferences.js` as a complete-file rewrite so start+end selects the real contiguous flattened span.

## Completion proof

A Chitas click must remain on Awtsmoos, render the exact native Hebrew pesukim from canonical chapter posts, show the ordinary reader/comments chrome, support arbitrary selected week/date, survive hard reload, and contain zero `chabad.org`/`externalHref`/`virtualStudy` behavior in the active Chitas path.
